subject: Help with x-axis scale when using time-stamps

messages.author: 785a750b71d25f23
messages.subject: Help with x-axis scale when using time-stamps
parts:
Hello,

I am in need of help with a graph I am trying to do ggplot2. It is an activity graph using the geom_tile() option (Please see image attached). The data is activity measurements from loggers attached to seabirds. I am only interested in the data corresponding to the night. But when I plot the graph, it doesn't plot just the night-time data (18:00 - 5:59) but also includes the day-times (6:00 - 17:59) even though there is no data for this part. I think it has to do with POSIX.ct timestamps that must include a date attached to the time (very bothersome). Therefore times before midnight have a different date to those after midnight, hence they are graphed separately. 

I have tried subtracting a day from the times after midnight, also reversing the scale. They have not worked. 

Does anyone a way of telling ggplot2 to ignore the date or another format for times that is compatible and would work? So that only the times in the data are graphed and in the order from dusk till dawn.

The graph instructions:

ggplot(wet, aes(x=(time), y=date, alpha=wet_count)) +geom_tile()+geom_path(aes(x=moonphasenew, alpha=NULL))


Thank you for any help you could provide,

Sebastian Cruz
Max Planck Institute for Ornithology
Radolfzell, Germany
